Package org.apache.juneau.commons.secret

Class InMemorySecretStore

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.commons.secret.InMemorySecretStore
All Implemented Interfaces:
SecretStore
public class InMemorySecretStore extends Object implements SecretStore
Built-in default SecretStore: a per-process, ConcurrentHashMap-backed key-to-secret map.

This is the zero-config store SecretStores.resolve(org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.BeanStore) falls back to when no store has been contributed. It is honest about its limits:

Process-local only. Secrets live in this JVM's heap and are gone when the process exits — this store is not persistent. Two separate JVMs (or two instances behind a load balancer) each hold their own map and do not see each other's secrets, so it is not cross-node. It is a convenience default and a test double, not a production secret backend; deployments that need durability or sharing must contribute a store backed by an external secret manager.

Defensive copies. store(java.lang.String, char[]) copies the supplied array and find(java.lang.String) returns a fresh copy, so the caller may zero its own arrays without disturbing the stored value and vice-versa. delete(java.lang.String) zeroes the retained array before dropping it. The value is never toString()'d, logged, or dumped.

Thread-safety. All operations are safe for concurrent invocation.

Since:
10.0.0
